title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The document outlines a formal decision made by the AI Office regarding the implementation or oversight of artificial intelligence initiatives within the organization. It specifies the key objectives, guidelines, and responsibilities that will guide AI development and deployment moving forward.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy document announces a vacancy for technology specialists in the AI office. It outlines the qualifications, responsibilities, and application process for these positions.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces a vacancy for the Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office, outlining the role’s responsibilities, required qualifications, and how to apply. It emphasizes the adviser’s duties to guide AI strategy, ensure responsible and ethical use, and provide scientific oversight for the organization’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The document addresses how to handle openings for legal officer positions, considering the use of AI tools to support or fill these roles. It outlines guidelines and best practices for integrating AI into the legal office while ensuring compliance with legal standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The document announces a vacancy for AI policy officers and outlines the responsibilities and qualifications needed for the role. It explains the application process and the expected duties of the new policy officers in overseeing AI governance within the organization.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing the proposed AI Act to ensure that its rules are based on solid scientific evidence and best practices. They evaluate technical standards, risk assessments, and regulatory frameworks to provide informed, evidence‑based recommendations for policymakers.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This document proposes a formal request to establish standardized guidelines for a specific area of AI development or deployment. It aims to create consistent definitions, practices, and regulatory measures to promote clarity, safety, and interoperability across the field.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The CoP Consultation Notice announces a new AI policy review and invites stakeholders to give feedback on proposed changes. It explains the consultation timeline, key policy areas under consideration, and how participants can submit their input.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document invites stakeholders to submit expressions of interest to form a Community of Practice focused on AI policy and governance. It outlines the purpose, scope, and participation requirements for building a collaborative network of experts.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy describes a step‑by‑step, iterative drafting process used by the community of practice, highlighting how drafts are repeatedly reviewed, revised, and refined based on feedback. It offers guidance on collaboration, stakeholder input, and transparent version control to ensure the final document aligns with shared objectives.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document offers a visual timeline that tracks the drafting process of the AI policy, highlighting each key stage from initial brainstorming to final approval. It shows when major decisions occurred and which teams were involved at every step.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: A preliminary set of guidelines for responsible AI development, outlining expectations for transparency, fairness, and safety. Stakeholders are invited to review and provide feedback so the Code can be refined before final adoption.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document presents the second draft of a code of practice that outlines principles and guidelines for responsible AI development and use. It serves as a framework for organizations to adopt best practices, promote transparency, accountability, and safety, and comply with evolving regulatory expectations.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document is the third draft of a Code of Practice, setting out guidelines for responsible and ethical use of AI technologies. It aims to promote transparency, safety, and accountability while encouraging innovation in AI development and deployment.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework for governing artificial intelligence. It aims to balance innovation with ethical safeguards to guide responsible AI development and use.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that outlines principles for the responsible development, deployment, and governance of artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes commitments from stakeholders to prioritize safety, transparency, fairness, and accountability while encouraging innovation and collaboration across sectors.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: The policy defines AI activities that are prohibited, including those that manipulate opinions, spread misinformation, or exploit personal data without consent. It requires organizations to avoid these practices and to implement safeguards to ensure AI is used responsibly and ethically.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy defines what constitutes an AI system, outlining key characteristics, capabilities, and the contexts in which AI is applied. It offers guidance for stakeholders to identify and classify AI technologies, ensuring a consistent understanding and approach to regulation.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines how the government will improve communication and collaboration for start‑ups to spur innovation. It proposes initiatives such as networking events, public‑private partnerships, and information‑sharing platforms to support early‑stage businesses.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that offers early‑stage technology companies across Europe access to high‑performance computing resources and expert support services. By providing shared infrastructure, training, and mentorship, the initiative aims to accelerate innovation and help start‑ups scale their solutions using advanced HPC capabilities.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This slideshow webinar provides an overview of risk management fundamentals, covering how to identify, assess, and prioritize potential risks. It offers practical tools and best practices to help participants anticipate, evaluate, and mitigate risks in their work or projects.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar discusses how to spot, assess, and reduce potential risks in AI projects, covering practical steps and common pitfalls. It also explains governance practices and monitoring tools that help teams stay compliant and secure while deploying AI systems.
